primer.armies.t: Each army has the same twelve warriors. You always see your own ranks. The enemy shows only a veiled figure with a ? until it fights, or you look at it. That is the whole game: guess well.
primer.board.p2: Move along the lanes, one piece per turn.
primer.board.p3: Every fifth round the two inner rings turn.
primer.board.t: This painted wheel is the board, the Chakravyuha. Every piece stands on a cell. Spokes run in towards the centre and rings run around it, and pieces travel along these lanes. Two armies face each other, one on each half. You arrange yours first, in secret, then the battle begins.
primer.moon.t: Warriors of the moon, painted in indigo. Their hour is the night: in full battles every Chandravansh strike lands at +1 after dark.
primer.rules.k: The rules, one at a time
primer.slides: Slides as far as the lane is open
primer.sun.t: Warriors of the sun, painted in vermilion. Their hour is the day: in full battles every Suryavansh strike lands at +1 while the sun is up.
rule.clash.t: When you strike, the two ranks are compared. The higher rank wins and the other piece is removed. When the ranks are equal, the battle setting decides: either the attacker wins with a cracked shield, or both fall. The hour and formations can add up to +2.
rule.end.t: If no piece falls for a long stretch, or the last round ends, the stronger army holds the field. Add up the ranks of the fighting pieces, with +5 for a fort whose gate still stands. The Intel button shows both sums.
rule.form.t: Fight together. Makara, the jaws: strike an enemy that another of your pieces already touches and you hit at +1. Padma, the lotus: a piece touched by two of its friends defends at +1. Hour and formation together never add more than +2.
rule.goal.t: Every army guards a Durg, its fort. Strike the enemy fort and its gate breaks. Strike it again and the fort falls, and the battle is yours. If the enemy has no move left at all, they must give up.
rule.hidden.t: You see your own ranks. An enemy piece shows only a veiled figure with a ? until it is revealed. A piece is revealed when it fights, when your Divyadrishti looks at it, or when a Rath runs two cells or more. Use the Intel button to see what is still hidden.
rule.move.t: On your turn, move one piece along the lanes. Most pieces step one cell. The Rath slides as far as the lane is open, and the Ashvarohi goes up to two cells. The Shataghni and the Durg never move. A piece may not shuttle between the same two cells more than three times in a row.
rule.shakti.t: Shakti is a row of lamps, five at most. You gain one for every piece you take, and both armies gain one when the sky turns. Spend it on an astra, once per battle, using your whole turn. No deity is ever a piece: the astras are only called.
rule.sky.t: In full battles the sky has two hours. By day, Suryavansh strikes land at +1. By night, Chandravansh strikes land at +1. The sky turns every fifth round. The top of the screen shows whose hour it is and how long it lasts.
rule.spy.t: The Chara is weak, but if it strikes first it kills the Senapati or the Maharathi, whatever the hour. Against anything else it loses. Guard your commanders from it.
rule.trap.t: The Shataghni is a trap. It never moves, and any piece that strikes it dies. Only the Yantrik, the engineer, can take it apart. So a piece that has never moved may be a trap or the fort. Send a cheap piece to find out, not a commander.
rule.wheel.t: On the Chakravyuha, every fifth round the two inner rings turn one cell clockwise. They carry whatever stands on them, and a piece carried round is revealed. Dashed rings show where each piece will land.
